01.event: Ravnai, while selling sesame, reports Shmuel's ruling that a witness and judge join; Ameimar praises it.
01.turn: Rav Ashi rebukes Ameimar for praising it just because his maternal grandfather did.
01.outcome: Rav Ashi says Rava already refuted the ruling.
01.summary: Ravnai happened to be selling sesame and reported Shmuel's ruling that a witness and a judge join together. Ameimar praised it as excellent. Rav Ashi mocked him for merely echoing his grandfather's praise and noted that Rava had already refuted the ruling.
01.missing: Little narrative event; mostly a chain of statements.

02.event: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field he worked and asked Rava about it.
02.turn: Rava asks who relinquished the onions to him, implying they were stolen.
02.outcome: Rava rules the woman is not betrothed for a handful, though a bundle would differ.
02.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions taken from the field he worked. He came to Rava to ask about her status. Rava asked who had given him the onions, ruling they were stolen and the betrothal invalid, though a whole bundle would be different.

03.event: Rav Asi left his demanding elderly mother for Eretz Yisrael, then learned she was following him and sought advice on leaving the Land.
03.turn: Rabbi Yochanan's cryptic blessing worried him, and Rabbi Elazar reassured him.
03.outcome: He heard her coffin was coming and said he would not have left had he known.
03.summary: Rav Asi's elderly mother kept asking for more, from jewelry to a husband as handsome as him, so he left for Eretz Yisrael. Hearing she followed, he asked Rabbi Yochanan whether he could leave to meet her and got an ambiguous blessing, which Rabbi Elazar read as permission. On the way he heard her coffin was coming and said he would not have left had he known.

04.event: A man's father left him three mustard branches; one broke and held nine kav of mustard, and its wood roofed a booth.
04.outcome: Wonder-tale told as proof of future abundance.
04.summary: In Shihin a man inherited three mustard stalks from his father. When one broke they found nine kav of mustard on it, and its wood roofed a potters' booth. Rabbi Shimon ben Tachlifa adds that his father left a cabbage stalk they climbed with a ladder.
04.missing: No turn; an anecdote of marvel, cited as illustration.

05.actor: Rava and Rav Adda bar Mattana
05.event: A divorced betrothed couple came before Rava, who separated them with an intermediary.
05.turn: Rav Adda objects from Evel Rabbati; Rava replies they are visibly familiar with each other.
05.summary: A divorced betrothed couple came before Rava. He placed an intermediary between them. Rav Adda bar Mattana objected that a woman divorced from betrothal is paid directly, but Rava said he could see these two were familiar with each other. A second version has Rav Adda urging the separation.

06.actor: A woman selling belts and a man
06.event: A man snatched a belt from a woman, proposing betrothal if he gave it back; she took it silently.
06.outcome: Rav Nachman says she may claim she took her own property, so not betrothed.
06.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man snatched one and asked if she would be betrothed to him if he gave it back. She took it and said nothing. Rav Nachman ruled she could say she was just taking her own property, so she is not betrothed.

07.event: On his deathbed Rabbi named Babylonian places and their sins, including Bireta DeSatya, who trapped fish on Shabbat and apostatized after excommunication.
07.turn: Birth of Rav Yehuda was announced.
07.outcome: No resolution; a list of prophetic remarks.
07.summary: Dying, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi described Babylonian towns: one of Ammonites, one of mamzerim, one where brothers swapped wives, and one whose people trapped fish on Shabbat, were excommunicated and apostatized. He ended by saying a child, Adda bar Ahava, was circumcised and Rav Yehuda was born that day.
07.missing: It is a list of prophecies more than a single story.

08.event: Ten men carried a woman out on a bier and had intercourse with her.
08.outcome: Used as evidence for a halakhic rule.
08.summary: Rav ruled that a woman may not be secluded even with ten immoral men. As evidence, there was an incident where ten men carried a woman out on a bier as if she were dead and abused her.
08.missing: Only a one-line incident, cited as proof.

09.event: A man told Rabban Gamliel he found an unobstructed orifice.
09.turn: Gamliel suggests he diverted his path and tells a parable of a man at a dark door.
09.outcome: Unresolved; suggests the man's claim does not prove non-virginity.
09.summary: A man came to Rabban Gamliel and said he had found his bride's orifice open. Gamliel asked if he had perhaps diverted, telling a parable of a man in the dark who finds a door open or locked depending on the angle. Another version says he asked if the man had intentionally diverted.

10.actor: A man giving a conditional divorce
10.event: A man said his betrothed would be divorced if he did not marry her by New Moon of Adar, then claimed he meant Nisan.
10.turn: His claim creates doubt over the divorce.
10.outcome: The Gemara notes the dispute of Abaye and Rava.
10.summary: A man told witnesses that if he did not marry his betrothed by the New Moon of Adar, this would be a bill of divorce. When the date came he said he meant Nisan. The Gemara asks whether this raises a concern, and says it is a dispute of Abaye and Rava.
10.missing: The case ends in a legal analysis.

11.actor: Mar Zutra and Rabbi Yehuda from India
11.event: Rabbi Yehuda, a convert without heirs, fell ill and Mar Zutra visited him.
11.turn: Mar Zutra saw Yehuda was dying and told the slave to take his shoes home, claiming the slave.
11.outcome: Yehuda died while Mar Zutra gained a slave.
11.summary: Rabbi Yehuda from India, a convert without heirs, grew ill and Mar Zutra visited. Seeing he was dying, Mar Zutra told Yehuda's slave to take his shoes to his house, acquiring the slave. One left to death and the other to life.

12.event: A woman holding a bag of documents was claimed against by heirs; she said she seized it before the owner died.
12.turn: Rav Nachman asks for witnesses and she has none.
12.outcome: He rules it is seizure after death and void.
12.summary: A woman held a bag of documents deposited with her. The heirs claimed it, but she said she had seized it while the owner lived. Rav Nachman asked for witnesses, and she had none, so he ruled it was seizure after death, which is nothing.

13.event: Rav Yehuda ruled in a case of a husband feeding his wife's branches to his animals.
13.summary: The judges of Pumbedita say Rav Yehuda acted in a case of a bundle of branches, treating the husband's use as consumption of his wife's property, consistent with his rule on forbidden produce.
13.missing: Only a thin report of a ruling.

15.event: Me'oret made her slave do three of the harmful acts and he died.
15.turn: Raised as an objection to Abaye.
15.outcome: Explained away as the slave being weak.
15.summary: Abaye said the six acts kill in order, weaken out of order. Objection: Me'oret made her slave do three and he died. Answer: he was weak.
15.missing: The anecdote is a single clause used in argument.

16.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and the Sages
16.event: The Sages sought to permit the Gibeonites in Rabbi's days.
16.turn: Rabbi objects that no one can permit the altar's share.
16.summary: In Rabbi's time the Sages wanted to permit the Gibeonites. Rabbi said that even if they permit the Jewish share, nobody can permit the altar's share.

17.event: Rabbi Tarfon helped his mother in and out of bed and boasted of honoring her in the study hall.
17.turn: The scholars say he has not reached half of honor, since he never endured her throwing a purse into the sea.
17.summary: Rabbi Tarfon bent down so his mother could climb on and off her bed, and boasted of it in the study hall. They told him he had not reached half the required honor: had she thrown his purse into the sea in front of him, would he have avoided shaming her?

18.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
18.event: Rabbi Yehoshua visited Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri to study, found him among trees, and stretched a vine between them.
18.turn: He asked about sowing near grapevines.
18.outcome: Rabbi Yochanan ruled permitted at ten cubits, forbidden beyond.
18.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua went to study with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and found him sitting among trees. He stretched a vine from tree to tree and asked about sowing there. Rabbi Yochanan said it was permitted at ten cubits and forbidden beyond.

19.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya
19.event: A widow came before Rav Yosef asking for sustenance, wine and silk.
19.outcome: She answers she needs it for him and his friends; implied she receives it.
19.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef asking for sustenance and wine, and he granted both. She also asked for silk garments. When he asked why, she said it was so she would not be ashamed before him and his colleagues.
19.missing: Whether silk was granted is implied.

20.actor: A betrothed couple and Rav Yosef
20.event: A betrothed man and pregnant woman came before Rav Yosef; she said it was his.
20.outcome: Rav Yosef rules no suspicion need be considered.
20.summary: A betrothed couple came before Rav Yosef, she pregnant and saying he was the father. He admitted it. Rav Yosef said there was no reason for concern since he concedes it and the halakha follows Rabban Gamliel.
20.missing: Passage cuts off mid-sentence; resolved in segment 5.
